content_sections.body_text: Scene: ‘I was walking to class.’ Then: (1) ‘First, it began to rain.’ (2) ‘Next, a strong gust turned my umbrella inside out.’ (3) ‘Then, I made the decision to wait in the library.’ (4) ‘Finally, I continued to class.’ Each numbered line has one event.
content_sections.title: Read four events

content_sections.body_text: Cover the numbers. Ask: What happened first? What happened next? Write 1–4 beside the four lines, then uncover the model. Circle made the decision. The general word pair is make a decision; in this past story, it becomes made the decision.
content_sections.title: Put the story in order

content_sections.body_text: Say: ‘I waited in the LIBRARY, not the café.’ LIBRARY is clearer and stronger because it corrects the place. Now say: ‘I waited at HOME, not the library.’ Make HOME strongest. Record both lines, replay, and circle the word that should sound strongest; compare it with the capital word.
content_sections.title: Make the new word strong

content_sections.body_text: Write one scene and four one-event lines. Use first, next, then, finally and made a decision. Number the lines before you speak. Record the story, hide it, and replay; write the four events you hear. Compare them with the numbered script. Check that one contrast word is strongest, then tell the story without reading.
content_sections.title: Write and tell a new story
